label: Qubit spectroscopy
axes: A one-dimensional sweep of drive frequency along the horizontal axis (a second, mirrored top axis restates the same sweep as detuning from the currently stored value, so it is a relative re-labelling of the same points, not new information). The vertical axis is a rotated readout quadrature in arbitrary signal units, sign convention chosen by the node. Each panel shows the measured sweep as a solid trace with the node's fitted resonance model overlaid as a dashed curve; the claim under judgement is the frequency at which that dashed curve peaks. A figure may be a single panel or a grid of independent per-qubit panels, each with its own vertical scale and its own sweep span.
correct_signature: Exactly one coherent bump dominates the trace: a run of many consecutive samples that leave the baseline together, rise smoothly to a crest and return, rather than one sample jumping alone.

The bump's width at half its height spans a clearly countable run of sample points - several times the point-to-point spacing - so the feature survives being read as a shape and not as a single reading.

The excursion stands clear of the baseline - crest or trough, whichever way this panel's readout sign puts it, both equally valid - by a clear multiple of the peak-to-peak spread of the off-resonance noise, and is visibly taller than the tallest isolated spike anywhere else in the same panel.
The dashed fit is centred on that bump and departs the baseline in the same direction the data does; its crest and the data's crest agree to well within the bump's own half-height width.
The fit's width is the same order as the data bump's width - it may read somewhat narrower than the visible hump, but it is never a hairline no wider than the sample spacing.
Away from the bump the trace is featureless on both sides and sits at the same level on each side, and the fit's flat asymptote lies on that same level rather than below or above the data floor.
Any competing excursion is either an isolated single-sample spike or a bump under half the main one's height and more than a couple of the main bump's linewidths away from it.

failure_appearance.wrong_peak: The dashed crest is latched onto an isolated spike that its immediate neighbours do not follow - the fit is a hairline standing on one sample - while a broader, smoothly-varying hump of comparable or greater height sits untouched elsewhere in the same panel with no fit over it. Observed: the coherent hump and the fitted needle are separated by many of the hump's own widths, and only the needle carries the dashed curve.
failure_appearance.no_signal: The trace is a uniform noise band across the entire sweep with no run of consecutive samples departing the baseline anywhere. Observed in two forms in this node: the panel carries no dashed curve at all (bare data), or the dashed curve is a flat baseline line carrying a hairline spike narrower than the sample spacing with nothing beneath it in the data.
failure_appearance.noisy: A bump is arguably present but its height above baseline is comparable to the peak-to-peak noise band, so its flanks are not separable from neighbouring scatter and several unrelated spikes reach similar heights. The dashed crest could be slid by a fraction of the bump width onto a different sample without the overlay looking any worse, and the fitted width is far narrower than the vague hump it claims to describe.
failure_appearance.feature_present_fit_failed: A clear coherent excursion is visible - a smooth multi-sample departure well clear of the noise band with recognisable flanks - yet no dashed fit is drawn over it at all, or the dashed curve stays flat on the baseline and ignores it. Observed once where the panel's only coherent excursion departed the baseline in the direction opposite to the one every fitted panel rises in, and the fit was simply absent.

abstain_when: The panel carries no dashed fit curve at all - there is nothing in the picture to test the numeric claim against, so report the missing overlay instead of passing or failing the run.
The sweep is clipped: the crest, or either flank of the candidate bump, runs into the edge of the plot frame, so its width, symmetry and one of its baselines cannot be seen.
The figure is a grid of small per-qubit panels and the panel the claim refers to cannot be identified from its title, or the traces and axis labels are not legible at the rendered size.
Two or more coherent bumps of comparable height and width are present and nothing visible in the picture distinguishes which one the node was meant to take.
One outlier sample stretches the vertical range so far that the noise band and any bump are compressed into a near-flat line, making relative height unreadable.
notes:
Evidence base is thin and single-source: five archived figures from one multi-qubit device family, all from one node version, opened read-only. As stated in the task, no whole run is archived as node-rejected for this family - but the per-run records carry a per-qubit fit success flag, and panels flagged unsuccessful are visually distinct (bare data with no dashed overlay). Every failure appearance written above except drift was therefore read off a real panel, not invented.

Drift is null deliberately: this family's figure has only a frequency axis and no repeat or time axis, so there is no way a single figure could show a feature migrating. Do not let a judge invent one from a sloping baseline - a tilted floor here is a background artefact, and mild baseline asymmetry appears in panels the node accepted and wrote from.

Most important maintainer warning: the node's own accept flag is NOT a reliable label for "the figure looks right". Across the runs opened, several panels flagged successful show a hairline fit standing on a single noise sample with no coherent bump underneath, and in one of them a genuine broad hump elsewhere in the panel was ignored. Those are exactly the false accepts this judge exists to catch, so the judge must be allowed to fail a figure whose fit the node accepted.

Calibration caution in the other direction: in panels that are genuinely good, the fitted curve is routinely somewhat narrower than the visible data hump, and this is normal for this node's model and background handling. Narrowness alone must never fail a run. The discriminator is whether a multi-sample coherent bump exists beneath the fit at all - a fit no wider than the sample spacing with only scatter under it is the failure; a fit that is merely tighter than a broad hump it is centred on is not.

Sweep spans differ by a large factor between runs and between panels of the same run, and the vertical scale is per-panel and may be entirely negative. Neither is evidence about correctness. Where the feature falls inside the window is set by whoever chose the sweep, so position in frame must never be used; judge only shape, relative height against the panel's own noise band, and agreement between the dashed crest and the data crest. The top detuning axis is a view-only restatement of the bottom axis - a bump away from its zero means the stored value is being corrected, which is the normal purpose of this measurement and is not by itself a defect.
